subject: Customer report: bursty token delivery on streaming / short-term remediation
messages:
From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@streamflow.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T22:14:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Bursty streaming tokens affecting support chat

Hi Laura,

Starting ~21:45 PDT tonight we saw our support chat streaming responses arrive in large bursts (0.50s of silence then 2s of rapid tokens). Some streams also stop mid-response and resume after several seconds. This is happening across multiple users and both web and mobile clients.

Impact: poor UX for support reps (hard to triage customer chats) and two escalations from enterprise customers.

What we tried: client reconnection, switching regions, forcing non-streaming calls for a subset of users (works but not acceptable at scale).

Attached: a short HAR + a token timing capture (streamflow-client-har.har).

Can you confirm whether any rollout or infra maintenance occurred in us-west-2 around that window?

Thanks,
Ethan
Head of Platform, StreamFlow

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@streamflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T22:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Bursty streaming tokens affecting support chat

Hi Ethan we're on it. Thanks for the HAR and the timing capture. No scheduled deploys for the streaming fleet in us-west-2 during that window.

Short-term playbook you can apply immediately (safe, reversible):
- Enable a client-side fallback to short polling at 300ms for new sessions (keeps latency reasonable while we triage).
- Reduce per-connection streaming concurrency to 6.
- If you can, temporarily route a small percentage of traffic to your eu-west-1 tenants while we validate server-side mitigations.

We're activating a runtime triage now (looping in Karthik). I'll post updates every 60 minutes until resolved. If you want a call, I'm available in 20 minutes.

Laura
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachment: runbook-external-fallbacks.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T22:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Bursty streaming tokens affecting support chat

FYI moving to triage: StreamFlow (prod us-west-2) reports bursty token delivery + intermittent mid-stream pauses. Customer trace attached. Prior incidents pointed to KV cache rewarm and intermittent worker churn but do not assume same root cause.

What's needed: fast hypothesis triage (metrics + heap), temp warm-pinning for a narrow segment, and a short customer note with recommended fallbacks. Customer is sensitive due to enterprise escalations.

Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@streamflow.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T00:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Bursty streaming tokens affecting support chat

Triage summary (preliminary):
- Observed symptom: elevated tail latency on streaming workers with token delivery exhibiting batching behavior (small windows of backpressure then burst emission).
- Metrics: uplink queue depth increased on edge shard 7 at 21:42 PST, worker restart rate spiked for two pods, and KV cache hit ratio dropped ~22% on the affected shard. Attached edge-pod-metrics.csv.
- Hypothesis: a GC pause combined with a concurrent small-heap reallocation pattern caused momentary worker stalls; autoscaler reacted and terminated pods during the stall window creating cold rewarm for the KV cache and attention kernels.

Immediate actions applied (00:05 UTC):
1) Pinned 10% of StreamFlow traffic to an already-warm pool for 45 minutes (temp-warm-pinning.log).
2) Disabled scale-in for the streaming pool in us-west-2 for 2 hours.
3) Tuned prefetch so KV rewarm is incremental rather than bulk.

Customer guidance: follow Laura's client fallbacks. We'll follow with a patch to the cache allocator tomorrow.

Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@streamflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T01:05:00-07:00
Subject: Update: short-term mitigations applied, next steps

Ethan quick update: we've applied the warm-pinning and disabled scale-in for the pool. Your team should see a marked reduction in burstiness within minutes; please confirm with a few test sessions.

Next steps we are scheduling:
- Full heap and allocation trace review (target ETA: 2026-08-05).
- Code patch to limit burst allocations in the KV cache (staging rollout 2026-08-06).
- Follow-up call to review RCA and validate on your staging traffic: proposed 2026-08-06 09:00 PDT.

If the problem persists after warm-pinning, we'll open an expanded incident and provide a formal RCA.

Best,
Laura

From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@streamflow.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Update: short-term mitigations applied, next steps

Hi Laura,

Confirming: after the warm-pinning and client fallbacks the burstiness dropped significantly and our support reps report normal behaviour for the last 8 hours. We'll join the 2026-08-06 call to validate the patch on staging.

Also: wed like the postmortem for our procurement team (for SLA credits/impact summary). Please include exact impact window, mitigations applied, and next milestones.

Thanks for the rapid response.
Ethan
